searches.reason: Current sampled training margins cannot explain top-ten failures, particularly in Electronics. Seek a bounded, training-only audit comparing uniform, popularity-matched, and text-similar negatives against chunked full-catalog ranks. Measure rank stability and difficulty by item frequency and history length; label fitted-target results explicitly and keep the pinned evaluator unchanged. Require explicit dataset routing and panel coverage before reporting any four-category macro.

searches.reason: Move from descriptive history sensitivity toward identifying which model components support useful ranking. Seek paired activation interventions and component ablations that distinguish item identity, position, final-item dependence, and earlier-history integration, with unchanged-input and matched-random controls. Test a small, predefined component-specific training intervention prospectively; attention weights or sensitivity alone should not establish an explanation or improvement.

searches.reason: Turn qualitative complaints about broad relevance, redundancy, and uncertain item identification into an evidence-grounded diagnostic taxonomy. Use permitted titles, descriptions, histories, and timestamps to measure observable textual repetition and recent-versus-isolated support; require explicit feedback evidence for judgments about compatibility, ownership, or preference. Seek annotation agreement, abstention, and calibration methods suitable for twenty feedback users, keeping feedback summaries separate from macro validation HR@10.
